# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 7 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 7

---

**7:1** I too am mortal like everyone else, a descendant of the first-formed child of earth; and in my mother's womb I was shaped into flesh,

**7:2** over a period of ten months, formed in blood from the seed of a man and the pleasure that accompanies sleep in marriage.

**7:3** I too, at birth, drew in the common air and fell upon the kindred earth; my first sound, like that of all others, was a cry.

**7:4** I was nurtured in swaddling clothes and tended with care.

**7:5** For no king has had any other beginning of existence;

**7:6** there is but one way into life for all, and one way out.

**7:7** Therefore I prayed, and understanding was given to me; I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.

**7:8** I valued her more than scepters and thrones, and I counted riches as nothing beside her.

**7:9** I placed no precious stone on a level with her; for all the gold in the world beside her is a handful of sand, and silver is no more than clay before her.

**7:10** I loved her more than health and beauty, and I chose to have her rather than light, because her shining is unquenchable.

**7:11** All good things came to me in her company, and through her hands came riches without number.

**7:12** And I rejoiced in all of these, because wisdom was their guide; but I did not know then that she was the mother of them all.

**7:13** What I learned unselfishly I share unsparingly, and I do not hoard her wealth;

**7:14** for she is an inexhaustible treasure for human beings, and those who draw from it win for themselves friendship with God, commended to him through the gifts that instruction brings.

**7:15** May God grant me to speak with judgment, and to think thoughts worthy of what I have received; for he is both the guide of wisdom and the one who keeps the wise on course.

**7:16** For we are in his hand — we ourselves, and our words, and all our prudence and skill.

**7:17** For it was he who gave me true knowledge of what exists: the structure of the world and the operation of the elements;

**7:18** the beginning, end, and midpoint of times; the changes of the solstices and the turning of the seasons;

**7:19** the cycles of the year and the positions of the stars;

**7:20** the natures of living creatures and the instincts of wild beasts; the powers of spirits and the reasoning of human beings; the varieties of plants and the healing properties of roots.

**7:21** All that is hidden and all that is manifest I came to know; for wisdom, the designer of all things, was my teacher.

**7:22** For in wisdom there is a spirit that is intelligent, holy, unique in its kind, manifold, subtle, mobile, lucid, undefiled, distinct, beyond all harm, loving what is good, keen, free in action, beneficent, humane,

**7:23** steadfast, sure, free from anxiety, all-powerful, all-seeing, penetrating through all spirits that are intelligent, pure, and altogether subtle.

**7:24** For wisdom is more mobile than any movement; by reason of her purity she pervades and penetrates all things.

**7:25** For she is a breath of the power of God, and a pure outflowing of the glory of the Almighty; therefore nothing defiled can find its way into her.

**7:26** For she is a reflection of the eternal light, a spotless mirror of the activity of God, and an image of his goodness.

**7:27** Though she is only one, she is capable of all things; remaining within herself, she renews everything; age after age she passes into holy souls and makes them friends of God and prophets.

**7:28** For God loves nothing so much as the one who dwells with wisdom.

**7:29** She is more beautiful than the sun and surpasses every constellation; compared to daylight, she is found to be superior,

**7:30** for night succeeds to day, but against wisdom evil never prevails.

---

## Council Notes

**On 7:2 — "pleasure of sleep" vs. "pleasure that accompanies sleep in marriage":** EMET "pleasure of sleep that goes with marriage," LOGOS "pleasure that accompanies sleep in marriage," PNEUMA "pleasure that belongs to sleep and marriage." SOPHIA adopts LOGOS — most natural reading; the Greek hēdonēn hypnou refers specifically to the marital pleasure of the conjugal night.

**On 7:10 — "radiance never ceases" vs. "shining is unquenchable":** EMET "radiance never ceases," LOGOS "shining is unquenchable," PNEUMA "light never goes out." SOPHIA adopts "shining is unquenchable" — to phōs autēs ou sbennytai means literally "her light is not quenched"; "unquenchable" is the most precise English term.

**On 7:13 — "without guile" vs. "unselfishly":** EMET "without guile" (adolōs), LOGOS "unselfishly," PNEUMA "without holding anything back." SOPHIA adopts "unselfishly" — adolōs means without deceit/free from guile; in context the meaning is generosity of sharing, not mere absence of deception; "unselfishly" captures the moral tone better.

**On 7:20 — "virtues of roots" vs. "healing properties of roots":** EMET "virtues of roots" (dunameis), LOGOS "healing properties of roots," PNEUMA "medicinal properties of roots." SOPHIA adopts "healing properties of roots" — dunameōn rhizōn in this natural-science context means the powers/properties of roots, specifically their medicinal use; "virtues" (EMET) is archaic.

**On 7:22–23 — the 21 attributes:** All agents preserve the list structure without artificial connectives. SOPHIA adopts LOGOS's rendering of the individual terms as most precise. Key rulings: monogenes = "unique in its kind"; philanthrōpon = "humane"; amerimnon = "free from anxiety"; panepiskopon = "all-seeing."

**On 7:25 — atmis/aporroia rendering:** EMET "breath/emanation," LOGOS "breath/outflowing," PNEUMA "breath/pure stream." SOPHIA adopts "breath of the power of God" and "pure outflowing" (LOGOS) — atmis is specifically vapor/breath (not merely spirit); aporroia is a Stoic-Platonic technical term for an emanation flowing out from its source.

**On 7:26 — three images:** SOPHIA preserves all three distinct images: apaugasma = "reflection of eternal light" (not mere "brightness" — it is the reflected/radiated gleam); esoptron = "spotless mirror" (exact); eikōn = "image of his goodness" (exact). These three are philosophically non-interchangeable and must remain distinct.

**On 7:30 — "evil does not prevail" vs. "evil never prevails":** EMET "evil does not prevail," LOGOS "evil never prevails," PNEUMA "nothing overpowers wisdom." SOPHIA adopts "evil never prevails" — LOGOS's "never" makes the universal negation explicit; PNEUMA's expansion to "nothing" loses the specific contrast between wickedness and wisdom.
